Implemented the fix in django/db/models/sql/query.py.

Change: In `Query.get_aggregation()`, added `or self.contains_over_clause` to the condition that decides whether aggregation must be performed via a subquery (AggregateQuery over a cloned inner query). This ensures that when a queryset contains a Window function annotation (an over clause), the aggregate is computed over the windowed results in an outer query rather than being inlined into the same SELECT, which previously produced the PostgreSQL error "aggregate function calls cannot contain window function calls".

Verification: Ran the scoped public regression selection ("aggregation") — 124 tests ran, all passed (returncode 0). Note that public regression success does not guarantee host feature acceptance, which is run separately by the host.
